summary: Elk House is a 24.4 m (80 ft) light steel tower with a 1957 cupola; towermen entries for it span 1957-2002, and no source describes the site today.

notes_for_editor: No build date appears in any source read, so none is recorded. The 1957 cupola, 80 ft height and light steel design come from the websiteservice listing, which has no construction year for Elk House. Staffing comes from a towermen list that credits Maurice Bourassa's efforts for its information; its entries give years and tower names, not always the tower dates for each tower. The 'all towers condemned' line dates to 2001 and does not name Elk House, so it appears in the story only as a caveat and is not recorded as an event. Staffing status is set to unknown with as_of 2002, the latest Elk House entry (Joan Pelech 2000-2002). Agency is not recorded: no page read ties Elk House to the Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency or to the Department of Natural Resources; the NHLR page names the SPSA for North Cabin only. Access and status are left unset because no source says whether the tower stands or whether the site is open. The NHLR North Cabin page is cited only for the provincial camera-monitoring statement, not as a claim about Elk House. Searches used: 2. Firelookout.ca lookout pages returned no record data (the index loads by script).
